ground_truth_kind.description: How the correct answers this plan grades against were produced: labelled by a person, labelled by another AI/agent, or derived mechanically (e.g. a deterministic oracle or replay). Required when stage is gate; optional otherwise.

subject_identity.description: The identity of the classifier or service actually graded by this plan's results -- its name and the exact version under evaluation (the counterpart, on the spec side, of quoin-measurement's MeasurementCollection subject/tool_version fields on the evidence side). Optional, but recommended on every plan and especially on gate-stage plans, so a pass/fail decision can be traced back to what was actually tested.

preregistration.description: Tamper evidence only, not an ordering proof (PLAT-936). `bar_digest` is a sha256 digest over the normalized text of this document's own "Comparison and Enforcement" section, checked at measurement intake against that section as the document reads at admission time. A mismatch means the section was edited after the digest was recorded, and the collection is refused. This does NOT prove the bar predates any result -- a commit's author-date and a collection's own timestamp are both self-reported strings nobody attests independently, which is why the ordering check originally proposed for this was found unbuildable (PLAT-935). It also does not stop an evaluator reporting only a favourable pre-registered variant, does not stop a repeated re-run until one passes, and does not stop editing an unprotected input such as the baseline instead of the bar text itself. Optional.

bar_digest.description: sha256 of the "Comparison and Enforcement" section's text, normalized (CRLF to LF, each line's trailing whitespace trimmed, leading and trailing blank lines dropped) before hashing.

relationships.description: Structural links to other spec artifacts. When a pass/fail decision genuinely depends on more than one metric succeeding together (a composite/AND gate), that composition MUST be expressed here as one `references` entry per constituent metric's MeasurementPlan -- never as a fabricated single `metric` id, and never only as prose. Do not add a separate constituent-metrics field for this; `references` is the one spelling of the edge.

type.description: `measures`: this plan measures the target directly (e.g. the AssuranceProfile it informs). `references`: this plan points at a related artifact without measuring it, including -- for a composite/gate-stage decision -- each constituent metric's MeasurementPlan that the decision composes.

minimum_population.description: The smallest population size below which a result must not be trusted -- e.g. refuses the 'decided from two examples' failure mode. Optional; when set, a result collected against a smaller population is invalid and must be refused or flagged, not silently accepted.

repetitions.description: How many repeat runs are required before a result counts. For a gate-stage plan this is the standard repeat-count (e.g. 'passes 3 of 5 tries' is expressed as repetitions: 5 plus the pass threshold in decision_rule) -- it is not a separate field, so do not add a parallel required_repeats.
